issues.legal_issue: Whether jointly owned agricultural operations conducted through a common manager constituted a partnership or a co-ownership concern.
material_facts: Two owners held agricultural land in unequal shares and jointly cultivated it through a common manager appointed for convenience of management.
The record showed no agreement between the owners to form a partnership and no facts establishing that either owner acted as agent for the other.
The owners shared the profits in proportion to their ownership shares; the appointment of the common manager and the sharing of profits were consistent with co-ownership as well as partnership.
The concern was described as a firm in a printed return, but the return provided no separate option for a co-ownership concern.
issues.conclusion: The concern was a co-ownership concern, not a partnership. The appointment of a common manager, sharing profits or losses in proportion to ownership shares, and describing the concern as a firm did not establish a partnership on these facts.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, partnership is a relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all; the definition of firm in section 2(k) of the Bihar Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1948 takes its meaning from that Act. Partnership requires agreement and agency between partners, whereas co-ownership does not necessarily arise from agreement or involve community of profit or loss, and a co-owner may transfer an interest without the consent of the other co-owner. As discussed in Lindley on Partnership, these are material distinctions. A common manager and profit-sharing in proportion to ownership are not, by themselves, decisive evidence of partnership.

rule.if: agricultural_tax_classification_case and jointly_owned_agricultural_property and coowners_appointed_common_manager and no_partnership_agreement_evidenced and no_agency_between_owners_evidenced

predicates.agricultural_tax_classification_case: The proceeding concerns whether agricultural operations are taxable as a partnership or as a co-ownership concern.
predicates.jointly_owned_agricultural_property: Two or more persons jointly own agricultural property used to derive agricultural income.
predicates.coowners_appointed_common_manager: The co-owners appointed a common manager to conduct or manage the agricultural operations.
predicates.no_partnership_agreement_evidenced: The record contains no evidence that the co-owners agreed to form a partnership.
predicates.no_agency_between_owners_evidenced: The record contains no evidence that one co-owner acted as agent for the other.

issues.definition: When an agricultural tax classification case concerns jointly owned agricultural property managed by a common manager, and the record shows neither an agreement to form a partnership nor agency between the owners, the concern is treated as co-ownership rather than partnership.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a common manager holding agricultural land for persons jointly interested in it may be assessed for the tax payable by those persons when their concern is one of co-ownership.
material_facts: The owners jointly held interests in agricultural land and derived agricultural income from it.
They appointed a common manager to manage the agricultural operations on their behalf.
The concern was found to be co-ownership rather than partnership; the State conceded that the common-manager assessment provision applied if the concern was co-ownership.
issues.conclusion: The common manager was liable to assessment under section 13 in respect of the agricultural income tax payable by each co-owner.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Bihar Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1948 provides that where a common manager holds land from which agricultural income is derived on behalf of persons jointly interested in the land or its income, the aggregate of the tax payable by each person on the income derived from the land and received by that person is assessed on the common manager, who is deemed the assessee for and is liable to pay that tax. The Court noted that section 13 did not apply to a partnership firm.

predicates.common_manager_holds_land_for_jointly_in: A common manager holds or manages land on behalf of persons jointly interested in that land or its agricultural income.
predicates.agricultural_income_derived_from_that_la: Agricultural income is derived from the land managed on behalf of the jointly interested persons.
predicates.concern_is_coownership_not_partnership: The arrangement is one of co-ownership rather than partnership.

issues.definition: When agricultural income tax is assessed on income from land managed by a common manager for jointly interested co-owners, and their arrangement is co-ownership rather than partnership, the common manager is assessed for the owners' tax.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a finding that an arrangement is a partnership is conclusive when the decision-maker reached it by applying an incorrect legal test.
material_facts: The taxing authorities and the High Court treated the appointment of a common manager and the sharing of profits in proportion to the owners' shares as grounds for finding a partnership.
The record did not establish an agreement to form a partnership or an agency relationship between the owners.
The Court concluded that the partnership question had been assessed without applying the correct legal distinctions between partnership and co-ownership.
issues.conclusion: The finding was not conclusive because the partnership question was a mixed question of fact and law and the authorities had applied an incorrect legal principle.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a relationship is a partnership is ordinarily a question of fact but is a mixed question of fact and law where the decision-maker must apply the correct legal test. A factual finding reached after applying a wrong principle of law is not conclusive. The Court relied on Modern Rigg & Co. and R. B. Eskrigge & Co. v. Monks (1923) 8 T.C. 450.

predicates.partnership_classification_review: The proceeding reviews a determination whether a business or arrangement is a partnership.
predicates.decision_maker_applied_wrong_legal_test: The decision-maker assessed the relationship using a legal test that did not correctly distinguish partnership from co-ownership.

issues.definition: In a review of partnership classification, a finding reached using an incorrect legal test is not conclusive.
